If you sell digital products, these are 3 legal documents you need to know about, and most sellers completely overlook number 3 👀 1️⃣ Digital Product Purchase Agreement This can establish the terms of the purchase, including restrictions on sharing or reselling your digital product and other important purchase terms. 2️⃣ Website/Store Terms & Conditions Your Terms & Conditions establish the rules for your online business and can address things like refunds, intellectual property, and limitations of liability. 3️⃣ Content Usage License If a brand or client pays to use your videos, templates, graphics, courses, or other content, a content usage license can clearly define how they can use it, where, for how long, and what happens if they go beyond those rights. Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. 💅🏾 And no, you don't necessarily need to spend hundreds on legal fees just to get foundational documents in place. Do you desire to earn from digital products? You can start small, learn as you go, and build one helpful product at a time. 7 steps to get started 1. Choose a person you want to help.     Think about a group you understand—busy parents, new business owners, job seekers, or beginners learning a skill. 1. Find one problem they need solved.     Ask what they struggle with, search comments and questions online, and listen to the words they use. 1. Pick a simple digital product.     Start with something manageable: a checklist, planner, guide, template, short ebook, or mini-workshop. 1. Create a useful first version.     Make it clear, practical, and easy to use. You can use tools like Canva to design it, but the value comes from helping solve the problem. 1. Set a beginner-friendly price.     For a short guide or checklist, you might test $7–$17. For a more detailed workbook or template bundle, consider $17–$37. Check what similar products offer, then choose a price that fits your product and audience. 1. Choose a place to sell it.     Use a digital-product platform that lets customers pay and receive the file. Read its fees and terms before choosing. 1. Share helpful content and invite people to learn more.     Answer questions, show what your product helps with, and include a clear call to action. Keep improving based on feedback. You don’t need a huge audience to begin, but you do need a product that genuinely helps and a consistent way to reach people.
